newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Rockets kill six in Kabul, Taleban rebels advance.
newsitem.headline: Rockets kill six in Kabul, Taleban rebels advance.

text.p: Rockets slammed into Kabul on Monday killing six people and wounding 22, as Taleban rebels said they had gained ground east of the Afghan capital Kabul.
Government-controlled Kabul radio, monitored in Islamabad, said the Taleban militia had sent dozens of rockets crashing into residential areas overnight and during the day.
It said six people had been killed and 22 wounded, and several houses had been destroyed.
The Taleban has tightened its grip on eastern provinces this month as part of a drive to seize the capital, oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.
The radio said forces loyal to Rabbani had retaliated with artillery fire against Taleban positions just south of Kabul, but had no word on casualties there.
The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted a Taleban spokesman as saying the militia's fighters had moved to within 15 km (nine miles) of the government-held town of Sarobi on Monday.
Sarobi is a stronghold of Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami faction.
It controls access to the Tagab Valley -- a route for a possible assault on the government's main military airbase at Bagram, about 50 km (31 miles) north of Kabul.
The spokesman said the Taleban had pushed its opponents back towards Sarobi, 70 km (40 miles) east of Kabul, in a counter-attack after government troops made small gains in fighting on Sunday.
"We have advanced 15 to 20 km (nine to 13 miles) since yesterday," the spokesman told AIP.
He put Taleban casualties at four dead in the latest battle, but AIP said a higher number had been taken to Jalalabad, the eastern city captured by the Taleban on September 11.
There was no immediate word on government losses.
AIP said government troops had attacked Taleban positions near the town of Maidan Shahr, southwest of Kabul. The Taleban said it had repelled the assault after a three-hour battle.

A Taleban spokesman said earlier the militia's military chief, Mullah Borjan, was expected to move to the Sarobi front soon after mopping up government resistance in Kunar province on the Pakistani border, which fell to the rebels on Sunday.
No comment from the government side was immediately available and there was no independent account of the fighting for Sarobi, which lies on the main road to Kabul.
